sections.en:
1 In this Parma codex are found the same works as in the Venice codex 1,
ff. 187 ff., which perhaps was copied from it. — I doubt whether this book too by the hand
of Eleutherius the astrologer (see p. 6, n. 1) was written, nor did the prefect of the Parma
library, who through the mediation of Domenico Bassi compared a photographic image of the Turin
codex, dare to assert anything.

summary.headline: Palatine Codex 165 Contents
summary.text: Catalog entry for Palatine Library codex 165, a fourteenth-century paper manuscript listing works on solar obliquity, lunar and planetary relations, ascetic instruction, Ptolemy’s Tetrabiblos, the Hundred Chapters or “Fruits,” Paulus Alexandrinus’s introductory apotelesmatic methods, and Hyparchus on the zodiac signs. The entry also records astrological notes dated 1371 and 1374 and compares the manuscript with Florentine, Milanese, and Parma codices.
